s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulcerative lesion with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and heaped-up margins
Intracellular yeasts within histiocytes on histopathological examination
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years with oral hypoglycemic agents
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils on histopathological examination
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

shortlist.label: Chronic histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes, consistent with histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of intracellular yeasts, although less common than histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and chronic nature of the ulcer, although no definitive evidence of TB

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of epithelioid cells and giant cells, although less common in the oral cavity

shortlist.label: Chronic candidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of intracellular yeasts and chronic nature of the ulcer, although fungal culture was negative

rule_in.why: it is endemic in eastern India

rule_out.why: it is less common in eastern India

trace.fact: Chief complaint: nonhealing ulcer on the tongue

rule_in.why: it is more commonly associated with oral ulcers

rule_out.why: duration is compatible with all candidates

trace.fact: Initial lesion description: small painless mass
Lesion location: right lateral aspect of the tongue

rule_in.why: it often presents with oral lesions

rule_out.why: lesion location does not discriminate between candidates

trace.fact: Lesion progression: gradually grew and ulcerated

rule_in.why: it is more commonly associated with ulceration

rule_out.why: it does not typically cause ulcerating lesions
